extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in media, journalism ethics, and newsroom accountability (journalists, editors, media-watchers)
extracted.subtask_description: A news report describing an instance of alleged plagiarism by a reporter and the newsroom standards, responses, and disciplinary expectations that apply. Focuses on attribution, corrective notices, and severity of misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper attribution of material from other sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The Post’s policy that the use of material from other newspapers or sources must be properly attributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor’s note and newsroom policy require attribution when using material reported elsewhere; failure to attribute constitutes a lapse and requires apology and correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on taking information without attribution (plagiarism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking information without attribution is unethical and not in keeping with The Post's standards of journalism. There are no mitigating circumstances for plagiarism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism is described as "the most serious kind of matter for a news organization," implying zero tolerance and expectation of disciplinary measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective transparency: publish editor's note/apology
rubrics_metrics.description: When duplication or borrowing of material occurs, publish an editor's note acknowledging the issue and apologizing to affected outlets and readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Post posted an editor's note admitting that articles contained "substantial material that was borrowed and duplicated, without attribution" and apologized to the Arizona Republic and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary response: immediate, severe and appropriate action
rubrics_metrics.description: Newsroom response should include prompt and significant disciplinary steps when plagiarism is found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A spokesperson said "immediate, severe and appropriate" action was taken; personnel specifics may be withheld per internal policies but serious sanctions are expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope-of-copying as a factor in seriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent and nature of the copying (e.g., copying whole paragraphs vs. isolated facts) informs the severity of the lapse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: two paragraphs copied in one article; 10 of 15 paragraphs copied in another — showing that wholesale or repeated copying heightens the violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of previously reported facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when reporting facts (not just verbatim text), facts previously reported by another outlet should be attributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Post noted articles "included without attribution other facts previously reported by the Republic," indicating that paraphrased facts or reporting based on others' reporting require credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on disclosure of personnel actions
rubrics_metrics.description: News organizations may decline to disclose specific personnel actions while still asserting that appropriate measures were taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A spokesperson declined to elaborate on personnel consequences, citing a "longstanding policy of not discussing specific personnel actions," which is a procedural constraint on transparency regarding individual discipline.
